findings.name: Dual input mapping (keyboard+mouse and gamepad)
findings.statement: The game must expose one action set — move, lock on, pounce, dash, poop — bound simultaneously to keyboard+mouse (WASD, right-click, left-click, Space, Q) and gamepad (left stick, left trigger, A, right trigger, B), both treated as first-class.
findings.observable_behaviour: A player can perform every listed action with either device without entering a settings menu, and can swap mid-run: pressing Q and pressing B both poop the oldest colour; left-click and A both pounce.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs — `PlayerController` with moveSpeed, LockConeDot, OnLockTargetChanged, Update, string literal "target then launch"
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameManager.cs — `EnsureDesktopPointer`
Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs — WindupTime, PounceTime, isLockedByPlayer
No symbol anywhere referencing gamepad/joystick/Input System (no PlayerInput, InputAction, actions asset, no rebinding/device code)

No 'poop' / colour-buffer action symbol in PlayerController (no buffer, eject, or oldest-colour member); PlayerController literals are "upgrade_damage", "upgrade_speed", "upgrade_health", "gene_points"
findings.reasoning: Movement, lock-on and pounce clearly exist as gameplay (PlayerController.moveSpeed/LockConeDot/OnLockTargetChanged, EnemyAI.isLockedByPlayer/WindupTime/PounceTime), and GameManager.EnsureDesktopPointer plus the mouse-flavoured hint "target then launch" indicate the polling happens against keyboard+mouse in PlayerController.Update. However the inventory shows no Unity Input System artefacts at all — no InputAction/PlayerInput/actions-asset reference, no per-device abstraction, no gamepad/stick/trigger symbols — so there is no evidence any of the five actions is reachable from a controller, and nothing suggests a single shared action set exists as the design demands. Additionally one of the five listed actions, poop (Q / B), has no counterpart in the codebase: there is no colour-buffer or eject member on PlayerController, so that binding cannot exist on either device. Dash exists only as a stat multiplier (ClassProfile.dashMult, StatBlock.dash), not visibly as an input action. Note the inventory is declaration-only, so direct Input.GetKey/GetMouseButton calls inside Update bodies are invisible; the keyboard side is inferred, and the gamepad absence is inferred from the total lack of any device-abstraction declaration. Treat confidence as low on the exact keyboard coverage, higher on the gamepad gap.
findings.what_exists_instead: A single-device, hard-polled control path: PlayerController.Update reads keyboard/mouse directly (evidenced by EnsureDesktopPointer, LockConeDot, "target then launch"), with no action-set indirection and no controller path; the poop action does not exist on any device because the colour buffer is unimplemented.
findings.effort_reason: The gameplay verbs already exist as methods on PlayerController/EnemyAI, so the work is inserting an action-set layer (Input System asset or a small InputRouter returning move vector + five booleans) and repointing the existing Update polling at it — a localised refactor of one 521-line file rather than new systems. The medium rather than small rating is because the poop action has no underlying implementation (no colour-buffer member anywhere), so one of the five bindings has nothing to bind to until that system lands.

findings.name: Top-down movement and facing
findings.statement: The player beast moves in the top-down plane under WASD / left-stick input and always faces the direction it is moving.
findings.observable_behaviour: Holding a direction moves the cube-beast that way and rotates its front to match; releasing input stops it facing the last travel direction.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs — class PlayerController: moveSpeed, BaseSpeed, Awake, Update, gameStarted
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameManager.cs — creates "Player" GameObject, EnsureDesktopPointer
Assets/Scripts/Game/Creature.cs — GroundFollow, GroundY, StickY (keeps body on terrain plane)
Assets/Scripts/World/BiomeTerrain.cs — SampleHeight, HeightAt (ground plane for top-down traversal)
findings.reasoning: The core locomotion requirement is the most basic thing a 521-line PlayerController with `moveSpeed`, `BaseSpeed` and an `Update` loop would do, and the surrounding systems assume a moving player in a top-down plane: GameManager spawns a "Player" and a "Main Camera"/"MainCamera" rig, Creature exposes GroundFollow/GroundY/StickY to pin bodies to the terrain surface, and BiomeTerrain.SampleHeight/HeightAt provides the height field the mover would sample. Nothing in the inventory suggests a competing locomotion mechanism (no navmesh agent, no click-to-move controller, no CharacterController wrapper class). The one part I cannot confirm from a declarations-only index is the facing rule — there is no named symbol such as `faceSpeed`, `turnRate`, `facing` or `Rotate` in PlayerController, and the lock-on cone (`LockConeDot`, `OnLockTargetChanged`) implies a forward vector exists and is derived from something, most plausibly travel direction. Because `LockConeDot` is a dot-product threshold against a facing direction, a facing vector must be maintained somewhere in the player, which supports the requirement rather than contradicting it. Also note gamepad left-stick support is indistinguishable here: if the code reads Unity's "Horizontal"/"Vertical" axes, stick input works for free; if it reads Input.GetKey directly, only WASD works. Neither can be told from the index.
findings.what_exists_instead: A single monolithic PlayerController with moveSpeed/BaseSpeed and an Update loop drives the beast over a heightmapped BiomeTerrain, with Creature.GroundFollow/StickY keeping it on the surface; the lock-on cone (LockConeDot) consumes a forward/facing direction that the controller must be producing.
findings.effort_reason: If facing already tracks movement, zero work. If only the rotation half is missing, it is a few lines inside PlayerController.Update using the existing move vector, and no data or new type is needed; likewise, switching key reads to the "Horizontal"/"Vertical" axes would pick up left-stick support without any new code.

findings.name: Solid bodies and obstacles
findings.statement: Creatures and terrain obstacles are solid; neither the player nor creatures may pass through them.
findings.observable_behaviour: Walking into a standing creature or a rock stops the player rather than overlapping it; a pounce into a standing creature bounces the player back instead of passing through.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/Obstacle.cs (6 lines, `class Obstacle` — no members parsed; bare marker component)
Assets/Scripts/Game/Creature.cs — `GroundFollow`, `GroundY`, `StickY`, `Update` (transform/height-driven placement via terrain sample, no rigidbody/collider symbols)
Assets/Scripts/World/BiomeTerrain.cs — `SampleHeight`, `HeightAt` (ground is queried analytically, not collided against)
Assets/Scripts/World/PropScatter.cs — `Scatter`, `MeasureHeight`, `class PropSet` (props instantiated from art-manifest.json; no collider setup symbol)
Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs — `moveSpeed`, `Update`, `LockConeDot` (movement/lock/pounce driven from Update; no bounce/push-out/collision member)
Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs — `PounceLungeFactor`, `WindupTime`, `PounceTime` (pounce timing exists, no rebound symbol)
findings.reasoning: The design demands two solidity behaviours: (a) player and creatures cannot walk through creatures or obstacles, and (b) a pounce into a standing creature bounces the player back. The inventory shows the ingredients for the *topic* but no symbol that implements either rule. Movement looks kinematic and terrain-sampled (`Creature.GroundFollow`/`GroundY`/`StickY` plus `BiomeTerrain.SampleHeight`/`HeightAt`), which is a strong hint that positions are written directly to transforms rather than resolved against colliders — that style passes straight through other bodies unless explicit separation code exists, and none is named. There is an `Obstacle` marker class with zero members and a `Props` object created in GameManager, so obstacles are at least *tagged*, which is why this is not a clean ABSENT: some scaffolding for the concept exists. On the pounce side, `PounceLungeFactor`/`PounceTime` in EnemyAI and the lock/launch flow in PlayerController cover beats 1 and 2 of the three-beat rhythm, and `dizzy` knockdown is clearly present (`Creature`/`EnemyAI` string literals "dizzy", `DownedDuration`), but no rebound/knockback member appears anywhere. Caveat: this inventory indexes declarations only, so `gameObject.AddComponent<CapsuleCollider>()` or a `Physics.ComputePenetration` call inside `Creature.Awake`/`BuildVisuals`, `PropScatter.Scatter`, or `PlayerController.Update` would be invisible here. Hence low confidence — the honest reading is 'concept tagged, enforcement unverifiable and probably missing'.
findings.what_exists_instead: Transform/height-driven kinematic movement: creatures snap to terrain via `GroundFollow`/`StickY` against `BiomeTerrain.SampleHeight`, the player moves by `moveSpeed` in `Update`, and obstacles are only marked by an empty `Obstacle` component on props scattered by `PropScatter`. Pounce exists as timed lunge state (`PounceTime`, `PounceLungeFactor`) that ends in damage/knockdown (`TakeDamage`, `DownedDuration`, "dizzy") with no rebound.
findings.effort_reason: Mostly additive: colliders can be attached at the existing creation points (`Creature.BuildVisuals`, `PropScatter.Scatter`, which already computes `MeasureHeight` for sizing and so already knows prop extents), and the `Obstacle` marker is already in place to identify blockers. The real work is that movement is written straight to transforms alongside `GroundFollow`/`StickY` ground snapping, so `PlayerController.Update` and `Creature.Update` need a depenetration/blocked-move step (or a CharacterController) that must coexist with the terrain-height snap — modification of existing movement code, not deletion. The pounce bounce is a small add on top: the lunge already has a discrete `PounceTime` window and a hit path through `TakeDamage`, so reversing velocity on a standing-target hit is a few lines once collision is detected.

findings.name: Lock-on targeting
findings.statement: Holding right-click / left trigger locks the nearest creature inside the player's facing cone; lock range is a stat that grows as the player evolves, and the lock breaks if the target gets far enough away.
findings.observable_behaviour: A red ring snaps over the nearest creature ahead while the button is held; releasing or running away removes the ring. A higher-rank/longer-reach form locks targets that a one-limb blank could not.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs: `LockConeDot`, `OnLockTargetChanged`, string "target then launch"
Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs: `isLockedByPlayer`, string "targeted"
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameManager.cs: strings "LockReticleWorld", "LockReticle", "ThreatHaloWorld", "ThreatHalo", "You are targeted"
Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs fields: `BaseSpeed`, `BaseDamage`, `BaseHealth`, `level`, `ClassName` — no lock-range field
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs: `Ecology.SightRadius`, `Ecology.ReachScale`, `ClassProfile` (speedMult, damageMult, healthMult, lungeMult, dashMult) — no lock/target range multiplier
findings.what_exists_instead: A working lock-on subsystem exists: PlayerController exposes `LockConeDot` (a facing-cone dot-product threshold) and an `OnLockTargetChanged` event; GameManager builds a world-space `LockReticle`/`LockReticleWorld` ring object and EnemyAI carries `isLockedByPlayer` plus a "targeted" state, and the reciprocal threat halo (`ThreatHalo`, "You are targeted") is present. What is missing is the range side of the rule: neither PlayerController nor GameConfig.ClassProfile/Tiers expose any lock-range or target-range stat, and the only radius-like constants are ecology-side (`Ecology.SightRadius`, `SightJitter`) used for AI perception rather than the player's lock. So lock distance appears to be a fixed constant rather than a stat that grows with evolution; `Evolve` in PlayerController scales speed/damage/health via ClassProfile multipliers only.
findings.effort_reason:
The cone test, reticle, target-changed event and enemy lock flag already exist, so the gap is one scalar: add a lockRange field to PlayerController (or a lockRangeMult to `GameConfig.ClassProfile`, alongside lungeMult/dashMult which already scale per class) and multiply it in `Evolve`, then use it in the existing distance/break check. No existing mechanism conflicts, so nothing must be removed.satisely additive.
reasoning duplicated here for schema safety: lock-on cone targeting, red reticle and lock-broadcast are implemented, but the design's rule that lock range is a stat growing with evolution is not visible — no lock-range field on PlayerController and no lock/target-range multiplier in ClassProfile or TierData — hence partial rather than present.

findings.name: Pounce attack
findings.statement: Left-click / A launches the player at the locked creature with no charge meter; hitting a standing creature drains that creature's Health and bounces the player back.
findings.observable_behaviour: Pressing pounce while locked visibly leaps the beast at the target, the target's health drops, and the player recoils away from the impact.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs: `LockConeDot`, `OnLockTargetChanged`, `biteDamage`, `moveSpeed`, string "target then launch"
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs: `struct ClassProfile` — speedMult, damageMult, healthMult, `lungeMult`, dashMult
Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs: `isLockedByPlayer`, `TakeDamage`, `GetEaten`, `DownedDuration`, `PounceLungeFactor`, `WindupTime`, `PounceTime`
Assets/Scripts/Game/Creature.cs: `TakeDamage`, `isDowned`, `isDead`
findings.reasoning: The lock-then-launch loop clearly exists on the player side: `LockConeDot`/`OnLockTargetChanged` implement the facing-cone lock, the HUD hint string "target then launch" names the pounce action, `ClassProfile.lungeMult` is a per-class lunge scalar consumed by the player, and `biteDamage` plus `EnemyAI.TakeDamage` / `Creature.TakeDamage` supply the Health drain on a standing target. `EnemyAI.GetEaten` and `isDowned`/`DownedDuration` show the downed-then-eat follow-up also exists. There is no evidence of a charge meter anywhere (no charge/hold fields), which matches the design's "no charge meter". What I cannot see in a declarations-only index is the third clause: the player being **bounced back** off a solid body on impact. No recoil/knockback/impulse member appears on `PlayerController`, and the only lunge-physics-named symbol (`PounceLungeFactor`) sits on `EnemyAI`, i.e. the creature side. Recoil could plausibly be a few lines inside `PlayerController.Update` with no declaration of its own, so this is a genuine limit of the inventory rather than proof of absence. I therefore mark PARTIAL: the launch and damage beats are demonstrably implemented, the bounce-back is unverified.
findings.what_exists_instead: A player lock-and-lunge attack driven by `LockConeDot`/`OnLockTargetChanged` and `ClassProfile.lungeMult`, dealing `biteDamage` through `EnemyAI.TakeDamage`/`Creature.TakeDamage`, with a downed state (`isDowned`, `DownedDuration`) and a separate `GetEaten` path for eating a collapsed creature. No visible player-side recoil/knockback member.
findings.effort_reason: The lock, launch, and damage paths already exist as named members, so at most a recoil impulse needs adding at the existing impact/collision point in `PlayerController.Update`; `EnemyAI.PounceLungeFactor` shows the project already has a lunge-magnitude convention to mirror for the player's bounce-back.

findings.name: Knockdown / dizzy state
findings.statement: At zero Health a creature does not die but collapses into a dizzy state (squashed, spinning); if left too long it rises again at half health.
findings.observable_behaviour: A creature reduced to zero health flattens and spins in place instead of vanishing; if the player ignores it, it stands back up with a half-full health bar.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs: `class EnemyAI` — DownedDuration, isLockedByPlayer, WindupTime, PounceTime, TakeDamage, Die, GetEaten, Update
Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs: `enum State` declared, string literals "dizzy", "dizzy / vulnerable"
Assets/Scripts/Game/Creature.cs: `class Creature` — isDead, isDowned, health, maxHealth, TakeDamage, Die, string literal "dizzy"
Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs — pounce/lock flow (LockConeDot, OnLockTargetChanged) that would drive the eat-while-down beat
findings.reasoning: The knockdown beat is clearly implemented rather than absent: EnemyAI carries an explicit State machine with a `DownedDuration` constant (a timer for how long the downed state lasts), a distinct `GetEaten` entry point separate from `Die`, and HUD/label strings "dizzy" and "dizzy / vulnerable". Creature mirrors this with an `isDowned` flag alongside `isDead`. That is exactly the design's mechanism: zero health -> downed/dizzy -> pounce again to eat, or the timer expires. The two details I cannot confirm from a declaration-only index are (a) that the recovery restores exactly half of maxHealth rather than full, and (b) that the visual is squash + spin — both would live inside EnemyAI.Update / Creature.Update bodies, which the inventory does not expose. There is no counter-evidence of a different mechanism (no instant-death-only path is implied; `Die` coexists with `GetEaten` as the post-eat cleanup). So this reads as PRESENT with the half-health constant unverified rather than PARTIAL.
findings.what_exists_instead: EnemyAI implements a downed/dizzy state with DownedDuration timeout and a separate GetEaten path; Creature tracks isDowned distinctly from isDead.
findings.effort_reason: Nothing needs rewriting — the state machine, timer constant and eat-while-down path already exist. Any gap is a one-line check inside EnemyAI.Update (set health = maxHealth * 0.5f on recovery) and a squash/spin transform tween, both in code that already runs each frame.

findings.name: Eating a downed creature
findings.statement: Pouncing a creature that is already dizzy eats it, consuming the creature and applying its meat effect (colour+tier to the buffer for coloured prey, healing for grazers), with distinct visuals per meal type.
findings.observable_behaviour: A second pounce on a downed creature removes it from the world; prey meat visibly streams into one of the player's limbs, grazer meat dissolves into the body.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs: `GetEaten`, `DownedDuration`, `enum State`, `enum Attack` members `carriesColour`, `healsPlayerPct`, `ApplyContent`, literals "dizzy", "dizzy / vulnerable"
Assets/Scripts/Game/Creature.cs: `isDowned`, `isDead`, `TakeDamage`, `Die`, literal "dizzy"

Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs: `PounceTime`/lock symbols in EnemyAI (`WindupTime`, `PounceTime`, `isLockedByPlayer`), `RegisterKill`, `Evolve`, literals "upgrade_damage", "upgrade_speed", "upgrade_health", "gene_points"
Assets/Scripts/Content/ContentDatabase.cs: `GrazerWeight`, `TierIndex`, `ColorTypeFor`, tier literals "Pale","Dusk","Deep","Rage","Clash"
Assets/StreamingAssets/forms.json — read by NOTHING; `FormTable.Load`/`FormDef` exist but nothing invokes them per inventory
findings.reasoning: The knock-down/eat loop itself clearly exists: `EnemyAI` carries a `State` machine with a `DownedDuration` (matching "rises at half health if left too long"), a `GetEaten` method distinct from `Die`, and `Creature.isDowned` plus "dizzy" strings. Meal typing is at least partially modelled on the enemy side: the content-applied fields `carriesColour` and `healsPlayerPct` distinguish coloured prey from grazers, and `ContentDatabase` already parses tier names (`TierIndex`, "Pale"/"Dusk"/"Deep"/"Rage"/"Clash") and `GrazerWeight`. What is missing is the consuming half: no symbol anywhere resembles a colour/limb buffer, meat queue, or tier-into-limb push. `PlayerController` exposes only `totalKills`, `level`, `score`, `Evolve`, and upgrade tokens ("upgrade_damage", "upgrade_speed", "upgrade_health", "gene_points") — a kill-count/upgrade progression, not a buffer of eaten colours — and `forms.json` (132 KB, the 150 forms) is parsed by nobody, so the form resolution the meat is supposed to feed does not run. Likewise there is no evidence of the two distinct meal VFX (prey streaming into a limb vs grazer dissolving into the body); the only visual hooks are generic `BuildVisuals`, "_EMISSION"/"_EmissionColor" tinting in `Creature`/`GameManager`. So: eating a downed creature works, grazer healing is plumbed (`healsPlayerPct`), colour+tier-to-buffer and per-meal visuals are not.
findings.what_exists_instead: A downed/eat state machine in `EnemyAI` (`DownedDuration`, `GetEaten`, `carriesColour`, `healsPlayerPct`) feeding a kill-count progression on the player (`RegisterKill`, `totalKills`, `level`, `Evolve`, "gene_points"/"upgrade_*") rather than a colour+tier limb buffer; tier data is parsed in `ContentDatabase` but `forms.json` is unread, and no meal-specific VFX exist.
findings.effort_reason: The hard parts are already there and correctly named: the second-pounce/downed path (`GetEaten`, `DownedDuration`), the grazer-vs-prey discriminators (`healsPlayerPct`, `carriesColour`), and tier parsing (`TierIndex`, tier literals) — data already extracted but discarded at the player end. Remaining work is a limb colour buffer on `PlayerController` for `GetEaten` to push tier+colour into, wiring `FormTable.Load`/`forms.json` so the buffer resolves, and two small VFX branches; no existing system needs deleting for this requirement alone, though the gene_points/upgrade progression will collide with the buffer once forms drive stats.

findings.name: Dash
findings.statement: Space / right trigger performs a dash whose speed is the form's Speed multiplied by its family Dash multiplier.
findings.observable_behaviour: Pressing dash produces a burst of movement; a Red Leaper's dash visibly covers far more ground than a Yellow Brawler's.
findings.acceptance_test: Red family Dash multiplier 1.6 vs Yellow 0.8 — the Red form's dash is measurably twice the Yellow form's at equal rank.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs: class PlayerController — moveSpeed, biteDamage, BaseSpeed, BaseDamage, BaseHealth, LockConeDot, Awake, Update (no dash field, dash timer, dash cooldown, or dash-related literal anywhere)
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs: struct ClassProfile — name, speedMult, damageMult, healthMult, lungeMult, dashMult
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs class names: "Brawler", "Bruiser", "Leaper", "Sniper", "Skirmisher", "Stalker", "Apex", "Forager"
Assets/Scripts/Content/FormTable.cs: class StatBlock — health, damage, speed, reach, dash
Data contract: forms.json (132,668 bytes) — read by: NOTHING READS THIS FILE
Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs: PounceLungeFactor (lunge, not dash)
findings.reasoning: The dash action itself has no visible implementation. PlayerController exposes movement and pounce/lock members (moveSpeed, LockConeDot, BaseSpeed, OnLockTargetChanged) but no dash state at all — a dash needs cross-frame state (duration/cooldown/velocity) which would surface as fields in the index, and none appear; nor is there any dash-related string literal or method. What does exist is the *multiplier data* in two places, neither wired to a dash move: GameConfig.ClassProfile.dashMult sits in a hardcoded 8-entry class table (Brawler/Bruiser/Leaper/Sniper/Skirmisher/Stalker/Apex/Forager) rather than the GDD's five colour families, and FormTable.StatBlock.dash parses a per-form dash value from forms.json, which the inventory marks as read by nothing. So the design's formula input (Speed × family Dash) is half-present as dormant data while the verb it feeds is missing. Note the dependent rule in §2.3 — grazer flee speed pinned below every form's dash speed — is likewise unreachable since no dash speed is ever computed (EcosystemManager/ContentDatabase expose GrazerWeight/Wandering but nothing comparing flee speed to dash).
findings.what_exists_instead: Movement is plain steering via PlayerController.moveSpeed/BaseSpeed, and the burst-of-motion concept exists only as pounce/lunge (ClassProfile.lungeMult, EnemyAI.PounceLungeFactor). Dash multipliers exist as unused numbers in GameConfig.ClassProfile.dashMult and as an unread field FormTable.StatBlock.dash backed by the unconsumed forms.json.
findings.effort_reason: Purely additive: add input binding plus a short-duration velocity burst with cooldown in PlayerController.Update, then multiply BaseSpeed by a dash factor. Smaller than it looks because both data paths already exist — StatBlock.dash is already parsed by FormTable (only forms.json is unloaded), and ClassProfile already carries a dashMult field, so mostly the values need retabling to the five families (Yellow 0.8, Red 1.6, Blue 1.0, Purple 1.2, Grey 1.3) rather than new plumbing. Extra work comes from the §2.3 coupling: grazer flee speeds in creatures.json must be validated below the minimum dash speed, which currently has no comparison code.

findings.name: Single Health meter and permadeath
findings.statement: The player has exactly one meter, Health; when it reaches zero the bloodline ends and the run is over permanently.
findings.observable_behaviour: One bar is shown on the HUD and no second resource exists; taking lethal damage ends the run outright with no continue.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/GameManager.cs: string literals "HudBars", "HealthBar", "HEALTH", "EvolutionBar", "EVOLUTION", "GenTierLabel"

Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs: fields totalKills, level, score; methods RegisterKill, Evolve, Die; literals "LEVEL UP! RANK {level}", "EVOLVED — {classProfile.name.ToUpper()}!", "gene_points", "upgrade_damage", "upgrade_speed", "upgrade_health"
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs: EvoRequirement, LevelUpRequirement, Tiers, TierData(name, scale, limbs)
Assets/Scripts/Game/Creature.cs: maxHealth, health, isDead, isDowned, TakeDamage, Die, Evolve
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameManager.cs: "DeathPanel", "EXTINCT", "Score", "RestartButton", "NEW EVOLUTION"
findings.reasoning: The death half of the requirement is broadly satisfied: PlayerController.Die / Creature.Die lead to a DeathPanel ("EXTINCT") with only a restart path ("NEW EVOLUTION"), i.e. no continue. But the HUD explicitly builds a second resource meter alongside health: GameManager creates both a "HealthBar"/"HEALTH" and an "EvolutionBar"/"EVOLUTION" bar, backed by a genuine second progression currency — GameConfig.EvoRequirement and LevelUpRequirement, PlayerController.level/score/totalKills, RegisterKill feeding Evolve, plus "LEVEL UP! RANK {level}", "gene_points" and upgrade_damage/speed/health choices. That is an XP/levelling mechanism where the design mandates exactly one meter with rank changed only by breeding and eating changing form rather than granting levels. Code exists in this area but on different rules, so it must be reworked rather than merely extended.
findings.what_exists_instead: A two-bar HUD (HealthBar + EvolutionBar) driven by a kill-count XP system: RegisterKill accumulates toward GameConfig.EvoRequirement/LevelUpRequirement, triggering Evolve, tier/limb growth from GameConfig.Tiers, "LEVEL UP! RANK" notifications and gene_points upgrade_damage/speed/health picks. Permadeath itself is effectively in place via Die -> DeathPanel "EXTINCT" with only a restart button.
findings.effort_reason: Deleting the EvolutionBar HUD object in GameManager is small, but the second resource is wired through PlayerController (level, score, totalKills, RegisterKill, Evolve, gene_points/upgrade_* branches) and GameConfig (EvoRequirement, LevelUpRequirement, Tiers) and mirrored in Creature.Evolve, so rank progression has to be re-routed to breeding rather than simply removing a bar. Health plumbing itself (Creature.maxHealth/health/TakeDamage/Die) and the death panel already exist and are reusable.

findings.name: Grazers as the healing supply
findings.statement: Grazers are harmless, no-colour, limbless white herbivores scattered thinly in every biome; they never fight, bolt the instant they are locked, and eating one restores a chunk of current-maximum Health without changing the player's form. Their flee speed is authored below every form's dash speed, and they never count toward an Alpha's eat-count.
findings.observable_behaviour: Locking a grazer makes it run immediately; the player can always catch it by dashing regardless of current form; eating it refills part of the Health bar while the body and limb colours stay unchanged, and the Alpha prey counter does not increase.
findings.data_contract: creatures.json: role=grazer entries with no colour family, no meat tier, grazer flee speed, home biomes
findings.acceptance_test: Grazer flee speed in creatures.json must be lower than Speed × family Dash multiplier for every one of the 150 forms.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs: string literal "grazer", fields `role`, `carriesColour`, `healsPlayerPct`, `isLockedByPlayer`, `GetEaten`, `ApplyContent`
Assets/Scripts/Content/ContentDatabase.cs: `GrazerWeight`, `RollSpawn`, `ColorTypeFor`, literals "Grey"/"WHITE"
Assets/Scripts/Editor/ContentCheck.cs: `HasSpawn`, `RollSamples`, literal "(grazer)"

Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs: `RegenRate`, `Ecology.WanderPace`, `Ecology.SightRadius`, `EvoRequirement`
Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs: `RegisterKill`, `totalKills`, `Evolve`, `BaseHealth`

findings.observable_behaviour: When an enemy locks the player an orange halo pulses; sidestepping during a small enemy's stationary wind-up makes its pounce miss, hitting it during the wind-up cancels it, and sprinting away drops the halo. Larger enemies close distance while the halo is up.

So 'a halo warns you when locked', 'wind-up then pounce', and a hunter-limiting sight system (Ecology.SightRadius/SightJitter/MaxHunters, ClaimHunterSlot) are all present in some form. What I cannot see in the inventory is the size-conditional branch the design makes central: no symbol suggests a comparison of enemy scale/tier against the player to decide 'smaller attackers stand still to wind up' vs 'bigger ones keep closing while locked' — Creature exposes tier and GameConfig.TierData.scale, but nothing in EnemyAI names a size or tier comparison. findings.reasoning:
Both halves of the requirement have code behind them, but only one is clearly complete. The floating bar is unambiguous: EnemyAI builds a child object literally named "EnemyHealthBar" with "BG"/"Fill" children and computes `BarWidth`, alongside `TakeDamage`; that is a per-creature world-space bar driven by damage. Whether it appears only after damage is not recoverable from the index, but the machinery is there.

The flee half is where the gap sits. EnemyAI clearly has multiple behaviour states (`enum State`, members not recovered) plus a hunting-pressure system (`hunters`, `BeginHunterFrame`, `CountHunter`, `ClaimHunterSlot`, `Ecology.MaxHunters`) and role tags parsed from creatures.json ("prey", "grazer", "elite", "alpha", "apex") with `Ecology.TerritorialPreyShare`. That shape says avoidance/aggression is decided by authored role and by a territorial-prey fraction, not by comparing the creature's size to the player's. The GDD rule is relational — anything *smaller than the player* flees, anything its size or larger hunts — and the data to evaluate it exists (`Creature.tier`, `GameConfig.TierData.scale`, `PlayerController` level/evolution) but there is no visible symbol that performs that comparison to select flee vs. hunt. §2.3's narrower rule (grazers bolt the instant you lock them) does look served by the "grazer" role plus `isLockedByPlayer`.

PARTIAL rather than CONTRADICTED because a role-tagged ecology is compatible with the design elsewhere and the existing state machine is the right place to add the comparison — nothing here has to be torn out.
findings.what_exists_instead: A role- and hunter-slot-driven AI: creatures carry an authored `role` ("prey", "grazer", "elite", "alpha", "apex") from creatures.json, a `TerritorialPreyShare` fraction decides which prey stand their ground, and `MaxHunters`/`ClaimHunterSlot` throttles how many pursue at once. Missing is an explicit size/tier comparison against the player that forces smaller creatures into a flee state.
findings.effort_reason: The flee state almost certainly already exists inside EnemyAI's `enum State` (grazers must flee on lock per §2.3), and both operands of the missing comparison are already in memory — `Creature.tier` / `GameConfig.TierData.scale` on the enemy and the player's evolved size via PlayerController. The work is adding a size-vs-player predicate to the existing state selection in EnemyAI.Update and letting it override the role/territorial default; the health-bar half needs at most a guard so the bar stays hidden at full health.

findings.name: Procedural body rendering of forms
findings.statement: One procedural system renders all 150 bodies from the cube: the authored socket layout gives the silhouette (reading family), the number of limb-segments reads rank, and saturation reads tier; traits render on the cube's main face so limbs stay free for colour.
findings.observable_behaviour: Two forms of the same family at different ranks share a silhouette but differ in segment count; the same form at Pale vs Rage differs in saturation; a trait appears on the cube face, never on a limb.
findings.data_contract: forms.json socket layout per form
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/Creature.cs: `class Creature` — tier, colorType, hasBodyColor, bodyColor, BodyColor, body, limbs, BuildVisuals, Evolve
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs: `struct TierData` — name, scale, limbs; `GameConfig.Tiers`, `ClassFor`, `EvoRequirement`

Assets/StreamingAssets/forms.json (132,668 bytes) — read by: NOTHING READS THIS FILE
Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs `class Colors` — Red/Blue/Green/... FromName (flat named colours, no saturation ramp)
No Trait/TraitFace/socket symbols anywhere outside FormDef field names
findings.reasoning: There *is* a procedural body renderer: `Creature.BuildVisuals` builds a `body` plus a `limbs` collection and tints it from `bodyColor`/`colorType`, and the number of limbs and body scale come from `GameConfig.Tiers` (`struct TierData` — name, scale, limbs) driven by `Creature.tier`/`Evolve`. That is a different mechanism from the design: the design says limb-segment count reads *rank* (1→6, gained only by breeding), silhouette comes from the authored `socket_layout` per form, and *saturation* reads tier/intensity (Pale→Rage). In the code, tier is a Greek-letter progression tier (`Alpha/Beta/Gamma/Delta/Omega` in GameConfig) that drives both scale and limb count, so tier and rank are conflated and intensity/saturation is not represented at all — colours come from a fixed named palette (`Colors.FromName`, "RED"/"BLUE"/"GREEN") with no Pale/Dusk/Deep/Rage/Clash saturation ramp applied to bodies (ContentDatabase merely recognises those intensity strings for spawn/tier indexing). The authored data the requirement needs is parsed structurally — `FormDef.socket_layout`, `silhouette`, `saturation`, `family`, `rank` all exist as fields and `FormTable.Load` exists — but the inventory shows forms.json is read by nothing, so no form's socket layout ever reaches a renderer. Trait-on-main-face rendering (§2.6a) has no representation at all: no trait type, no face/decal symbols. So the area is implemented, but on tier-table rules rather than form/rank/intensity rules, and the existing tier→limbs path would have to be rewritten rather than extended.
findings.what_exists_instead: `Creature.BuildVisuals` builds a cube body plus limbs whose count and scale come from `GameConfig.Tiers` (`TierData.limbs`, `TierData.scale`) indexed by `Creature.tier` (Alpha…Omega), with a flat named-colour tint from `GameConfig.Colors.FromName`/`ContentDatabase.ColorTypeFor`. `FormDef` declares `socket_layout`, `silhouette`, `saturation`, `family` and `rank`, and `FormTable.Load` exists, but forms.json is unconsumed so none of it drives rendering. No trait-face rendering exists.
findings.effort_reason: Smaller than it looks on the data side: `FormDef` already declares socket_layout, silhouette, saturation, family and rank, and `FormTable.Load` exists — the parse is written and only the wiring (forms.json actually being read, and a form assigned to `Creature`) is missing. The real work is rewriting `Creature.BuildVisuals` to build limb segments from rank/socket_layout instead of `GameConfig.TierData.limbs`, adding a saturation ramp alongside `Colors.FromName`, and separating tier-scale from rank-limbs across `Creature.tier`/`Evolve` and callers. Trait-on-face rendering is genuinely new (no trait symbols exist), but is a single decal/material slot on the body mesh.

findings.name: Biome generation, terrain gates and per-run palette roll
findings.statement: Five procedurally generated biomes run Prairies → Wetlands → Mountains → Beach → Volcanic with escalating traversal gates (none; Fins over roughly half the map; Claws and Coat; Fins+Claws plus Heat vents; Fins+Claws+Coat+Heat), each holding one Alpha lair, and each biome's creature palette rolled per run from weights.
findings.observable_behaviour: Without Fins the player is stopped at Wetlands water and can see the land beyond it; two consecutive runs of the same biome contain different colour populations; the Volcanic biome cannot be traversed until all four traits are held.
findings.data_contract: biomes.json: terrain, gating traits, palette weights, min distinct colours, population/respawn, pocket count, Alpha roster, both gate thresholds
findings.acceptance_test: Trait-introduction count per biome is 0 → 1 → 2 → 1 → 0 across Prairies, Wetlands, Mountains, Beach, Volcanic.

Assets/Scripts/Game/GameConfig.cs: `class Boss` — `SpawnIntervalKills`, `ScaleMultiplier`, `HealthMultiplier`; EcosystemManager `OnBossSpawned`
findings.reasoning: Two of the requirement's three pillars are handled by a different mechanism than the design specifies, and the third is missing outright. (1) Per-run palette roll: this part looks genuinely implemented — ContentDatabase parses biomes.json and exposes RollSpawn/Weight/GrazerWeight/Wandering/Pocket, and the editor ContentCheck.RollSamples samples rolls across the five colour names, so weight-driven palette rolling exists. (2) The five-biome progression, however, is layered on top of a surviving legacy three-biome system: GameConfig still defines BiomeNeon/BiomeMagma/BiomeCrystal with BiomeData.enemyColors and EcosystemManager exposes LegacyBiomes, while biome change is an event/notification (OnBiomeRequest → OnBiomeChanged → "ENTERING {biome.name}") rather than the player physically traversing generated terrain. That legacy palette/visual-swap path must be deleted or rewritten, not extended. (3) Traversal gates are absent: BiomeTerrain has a single TerrainProfile.Prairies and only a height field (SampleHeight/HeightAt/Radius) — no water bodies, lava fields, cliff climbing, or cold zones, and no trait inventory (nothing named Fins/Claws/Coat/Heat; EnemyAI only knows a "trait_miniboss" role string and a carriesColour field, so eating a miniboss cannot grant a key). Consequently nothing can stop the player at Wetlands water or block Volcanic until four traits are held, and the 0→1→2→1→0 introduction count is unrepresented. Alpha lairs are also replaced by a kill-interval boss spawner (GameConfig.Boss.SpawnIntervalKills, OnBossSpawned) rather than one landmark lair per biome.
findings.what_exists_instead: A single Prairies-only procedural terrain (BiomeTerrain) plus an event-driven biome swap that recolours the world from a legacy three-biome table (Neon Grid / Magma Wastes / Crystal Forest via GameConfig.BiomeNeon/Magma/Crystal and VisualsForBiome, EcosystemManager.LegacyBiomes). Palette weight rolling from biomes.json genuinely exists (ContentDatabase.RollSpawn/Weight/GrazerWeight, verified by Editor ContentCheck.RollSamples). Alphas arrive as a kill-count boss spawn instead of a per-biome lair. No trait or gate concept exists at all beyond the "trait_miniboss" role tag in EnemyAI.
findings.effort_reason: Requires four new terrain profiles with gate geometry (water depth, climbable rock, cold band, lava/vents) in BiomeTerrain, a player trait inventory wired to EnemyAI's existing "trait_miniboss" role, gate-aware movement blocking, per-biome Alpha lair placement replacing GameConfig.Boss.SpawnIntervalKills, and deletion of the legacy three-biome visual table (BiomeNeon/BiomeMagma/BiomeCrystal, LegacyBiomes). Two things reduce the cost: biomes.json is already parsed and the palette-weight roll (RollSpawn/Weight/GrazerWeight, plus Wandering/Pocket split and PocketLeakChance) already satisfies the per-run roll clause, and the five biome ids already appear as literals in GameConfig — so gating fields likely already sit in biomes.json unread rather than needing new data authoring.

findings.name: Pockets, distance-based difficulty and lair placement
findings.statement: Ordinary creatures wander everywhere so a meal is always findable, but the population mix darkens with distance from the player's entrance; top-tier meat clusters in defended pockets that bite back with swarming packs and elites; the Alpha lair sits at the strong end; and the per-run roll can place an over-tier pocket (e.g. a Rage hollow in the Prairies).
findings.observable_behaviour: Walking away from the entrance meets progressively stronger creatures; the strongest meat is only inside pockets guarded by packs and elites; some runs contain a pocket holding meat above the biome's normal ceiling.
findings.data_contract: biomes.json: pocket count, palette weights, population/respawn

findings.reasoning: The pocket concept exists in code, but as a *probability of a spawn table*, not as a place. ContentDatabase splits each biome's roster into `Wandering` and `Pocket` lists and rolls from them via `RollSpawn`/`Weight`/`TierIndex`; EcosystemManager then mixes pocket stock into ordinary spawns through a single scalar, `PocketLeakChance`. That means top-tier meat can appear anywhere at some odds, which is the inverse of the design's rule that Clash/top tiers *never wander* and exist only inside guarded locations. Nothing in the inventory represents a pocket as a world region: no pocket-placement, pocket-count, pocket-radius, guard-pack or occupant-converge symbols; `FindSpawn` and `BiomeTerrain.Radius`/`SampleHeight` are the only positional hooks and there is no distance-from-entrance term, no entrance/spawn-point concept, and no per-distance tier or weight scaling anywhere (Ecology exposes only global ContactDamageScale/SpeedScale/SightRadius). Alpha placement is likewise implemented by a different mechanism: `GameConfig.Boss.SpawnIntervalKills` plus `EcosystemManager.OnBossSpawned` spawn the apex on a kill counter with stat multipliers, rather than seating one Alpha lair at the strong end of the map. Elites and trait minibosses exist as role tags on EnemyAI (`elite`, `trait_miniboss`, `alpha`), and hunter-claim logic (`ClaimHunterSlot`, `MaxHunters`) gives swarm-ish pressure, but these are per-creature behaviours, not pocket garrisons. A per-run seed exists (`runSeed`) and biomes.json is parsed, but no symbol suggests a rolled over-tier pocket (Rage hollow in Prairies) — `PocketLeakChance` is the closest thing and it leaks individuals, not a pocket above the biome ceiling.
findings.what_exists_instead: A non-spatial spawn-table model: creatures.json/biomes.json rosters split into Wandering vs Pocket pools, rolled by ContentDatabase.RollSpawn with weights and a TierIndex, and pocket stock bled into ordinary spawns by EcosystemManager.PocketLeakChance. Difficulty scaling is global (GameConfig.Ecology.*Scale, Tiers) rather than distance-based, and the Alpha/apex arrives on a kill-count timer (GameConfig.Boss.SpawnIntervalKills → OnBossSpawned) instead of occupying a lair placed at the strong end of the biome.
findings.effort_reason: The parsed data is largely reusable — ContentDatabase already separates Wandering/Pocket rosters, knows tier order via TierIndex, and biomes.json is loaded, so the tables need labelling into places rather than re-authoring. But the runtime model must be rewritten, not extended: PocketLeakChance-based mixing has to be replaced by spatial pocket sites (count, centre, radius) placed on BiomeTerrain, spawn selection in EcosystemManager.FindSpawn must become a function of distance from the run entrance, guard garrisons of elites/trait_miniboss must be attached to pocket sites, and the kill-count boss trigger (Boss.SpawnIntervalKills → OnBossSpawned) must be replaced by lair placement at the far/strong end plus a per-run over-tier pocket roll.

findings.name: Ambient rank rules
findings.statement: Spawned creature rank is stated data: prey spawn at the player's rank minus one (floored at 1), elites at the player's rank, Alphas at the player's rank always at Clash, and the Apex at rank 6 Clash.
findings.observable_behaviour: A three-limb player meets two-limb prey, three-limb elites and a three-limb Clash Alpha; a one-limb player still meets rank-1 prey rather than rank-0.
findings.data_contract: creatures.json rank field; biomes.json Alpha roster
findings.acceptance_test: Player rank 1 → prey rank 1 (floored); player rank 4 → prey rank 3, elites rank 4, Alpha rank 4 Clash.

findings.reasoning: Creature ranking and spawn selection are both implemented, but on different rules than the design states. Spawn choice goes through ContentDatabase.RollSpawn with weighted rolls (GrazerWeight/Weight) over biome rosters plus Wandering/Pocket lists and EcosystemManager.FindSpawn/PocketLeakChance — a probability-driven roster draw, not a deterministic 'prey = player rank − 1, elites = player rank, Alpha = player rank at Clash, Apex = rank 6 Clash' assignment. The size/power ladder that exists is GameConfig.Tiers (Alpha/Beta/Gamma/Delta/Omega with scale and limbs) driven by Creature.tier and by kill-count progression (EvoRequirement, LevelUpRequirement, PlayerController.level/totalKills, Creature.Evolve) — i.e. the player's 'rank' is an XP/kill level, and the boss is a periodic kill-interval spawn (Boss.SpawnIntervalKills) with flat multipliers rather than a same-rank Clash mirror-match. There is no symbol anywhere binding an enemy's rank to the player's current rank, no floor-at-1 clamp, and no Clash forcing for alphas: 'Clash' appears only as an intensity string inside ContentDatabase (alongside Pale/Dusk/Deep/Rage), most plausibly feeding TierIndex/ColorTypeFor for colour-type mapping. The rank field the design names lives on FormDef.rank in FormTable, and forms.json is read by nothing, so the stated rank data is not consumed at all. To satisfy the requirement, the tier/level ladder and the boss-interval spawn path would have to be reworked, not merely extended — hence CONTRADICTED rather than ABSENT.
findings.what_exists_instead: A weighted-roll spawn system (ContentDatabase.RollSpawn + EcosystemManager.FindSpawn/PocketLeakChance) over biome rosters, combined with a five-step legacy tier ladder (GameConfig.Tiers Alpha..Omega with scale/limbs) advanced by kill counts (EvoRequirement/LevelUpRequirement, PlayerController.level, Creature.Evolve), and a boss spawned every N kills with flat stat multipliers (GameConfig.Boss). Roles are tagged by string in EnemyAI.ApplyContent ("prey","grazer","elite","alpha","apex") but carry no rank arithmetic.
findings.effort_reason: Smaller than it looks in one respect: the role taxonomy already exists (EnemyAI.role with prey/grazer/elite/alpha/apex), ContentDatabase already parses creatures.json and already has TierIndex plus the Pale/Dusk/Deep/Rage/Clash intensity vocabulary, and a rank field already exists on FormDef — it is simply parsed into an unread table. The work is to expose a player rank (limb count) instead of the kill-based level, apply the per-role offset with a floor of 1 at spawn time in FindSpawn/ApplyContent, and force Clash for alpha/apex. But it also requires unwinding the GameConfig.Tiers/EvoRequirement kill-ladder and the Boss.SpawnIntervalKills path that currently own creature scaling, which touches Creature, PlayerController, EcosystemManager and GameConfig.

findings.name: Trait minibosses and the four traits
findings.statement: Four traits — Fins, Claws, Coat, Heat — exist only in the meat of four miniboss carriers (Pond-dweller in deep marsh hollows, Crag-holder on rocky outcrops, Shaggy grazer-hunter in the Mountains foothills, Vent-dweller at volcanic seams). Each is a territorial elite, several times tougher than ordinary prey, that fights back and does not flee; eating it grants its traversal permission (water, high ground, freezing peaks, lava).
findings.observable_behaviour: The only way past water is to find and eat the Pond-dweller; the miniboss stands its ground and takes many more pounces than normal prey, and the pocket's other occupants tend to converge during the fight. Four such fights occur per run.
findings.data_contract: creatures.json: which trait a creature's meat carries, role=elite/miniboss, home biome/placement
findings.acceptance_test: Coat carriers live in the Mountains foothills, below the lethal cold, so Coat is obtainable without first surviving the peaks.

findings.reasoning: The carrier half of the requirement is partly wired: EnemyAI recognises a role vocabulary that explicitly includes "trait_miniboss" alongside "elite"/"alpha"/"apex", and ApplyContent/role/carriesColour suggest creatures.json role and payload fields are parsed. Territorial, non-fleeing, converging-pack behaviour has plausible support (Ecology.TerritorialPreyShare, MaxHunters, hunters/ClaimHunterSlot, SightRadius), and toughness would come from content stats (hasContentStats on Creature, StatBlock). What is entirely missing is the payoff half: no symbol anywhere names Fins, Claws, Coat or Heat, there is no trait inventory or permission set on PlayerController (its only unlock strings are upgrade_damage/speed/health and gene_points), and the eat path (GetEaten -> RegisterKill) has no trait-grant hook. The gates themselves do not exist: BiomeTerrain exposes only a single Prairies TerrainProfile with height sampling and a ground colour — there is no water volume, lava field, cold/lethal-altitude zone, or climbable high-ground rule that a permission could unlock, so "the only way past water is to eat the Pond-dweller" cannot be true today. Nothing enforces the placement invariant either (no per-biome miniboss placement, no foothills-vs-peaks distinction, no guarantee of four fights per run; only LegacyBiomes/FindSpawn and PocketLeakChance are visible). The mechanism present is not a rival mechanism — it is the same role taxonomy with the trait payload and terrain gating unbuilt — so this is PARTIAL rather than CONTRADICTED. Note that carriesColour appears to be the Clash second-tone gift (§2.4b), not a trait, so it is not a mislabelled trait field.
findings.what_exists_instead: A role taxonomy in EnemyAI that already includes the literal "trait_miniboss" (plus elite/alpha/apex), applied from content via ApplyContent, with territorial/hunter-swarm tuning in GameConfig.Ecology and pocket-vs-wandering spawning in ContentDatabase. Eating a creature routes through EnemyAI.GetEaten -> PlayerController.RegisterKill and yields colour/tier and progression rewards only. Terrain is a single procedural Prairies height field with no water, lava, cold or climb regions, and the player has no trait/permission state.
findings.effort_reason: The recogniser for role=trait_miniboss already exists, so carrier identification is cheap. The expensive part is net-new: a player trait/permission set with a grant on GetEaten, four traversal gates that need terrain features BiomeTerrain does not generate (water bodies, lava seams, climbable high ground, a lethal-cold altitude band above a survivable foothills band — currently only TerrainProfile.Prairies with HeightAt/SampleHeight), movement enforcement against those regions, and a generator placement invariant guaranteeing one carrier per correct biome/elevation with Coat below the lethal band.

findings.name: Trait permanence, face rendering and inheritance
findings.statement: Traits are body, not limbs: they render on the main cubic face, and once acquired nothing in the run removes them — they survive mutation, are inherited in full by every offspring, and are lost only when the line dies.
findings.observable_behaviour: After a mutation that rewrites every limb colour, the gill slits / hooked ridges / matted shell / glowing seam are still on the face and the player can still cross the matching terrain; every offspring in a litter shows all traits the parent held; on death all four are gone next run.
findings.data_contract: Run state: set of held traits, separate from limb slots
findings.acceptance_test: Breeding can never remove a trait a later biome requires, so the breed-and-lose-a-trait soft-lock cannot occur.
evidence: Assets/Scripts/Game/PlayerController.cs — fields/methods: totalKills, level, score, BaseSpeed, BaseDamage, BaseHealth, ClassName, Evolve, RegisterKill, Die (no trait collection, no held-trait set)

Assets/Scripts/Game/EnemyAI.cs — string literal "trait_miniboss" and fields contentId, role, carriesColour, healsPlayerPct in ApplyContent (a trait-guardian role name is read from content, but nothing grants or stores a trait)

findings.reasoning: Nothing in the inventory models a trait at all. There is no held-trait set on the player or run state, no face-slot distinct from limb slots, no code path that preserves anything across Evolve (the mutation entry point in PlayerController/Creature), and no inheritance channel — Companion carries only `target` and `index`, so an offspring cannot receive parent traits. The only trace of the trait subsystem is the enemy role string "trait_miniboss" in EnemyAI.ApplyContent, i.e. the creature data apparently labels trait guardians but defeating one has nowhere to deposit a trait: EnemyAI's content fields are contentId/role/carriesColour/healsPlayerPct, and PlayerController.RegisterKill has no trait argument. Traversal gating on traits (crossing matching terrain) is likewise absent — BiomeTerrain exposes Build/SampleHeight/HeightAt/SetGroundColor with no passability check. This is ABSENT rather than CONTRADICTED: no rival mechanism occupies the space, so the permanence/inheritance rules are additive work, not a rewrite. Note the requirement's implied data is run state, not an asset file, so it is not UNCONSUMED; the unread panels.json belongs to §2.8.
findings.what_exists_instead: Only limb/body colour and tier state: Creature.colorType/bodyColor/limbs with Evolve() rebuilding visuals, PlayerController upgrades keyed on "upgrade_damage"/"upgrade_speed"/"upgrade_health" and "gene_points", and a bare Companion component for offspring. EnemyAI recognises a "trait_miniboss" role string but awards nothing persistent.
findings.effort_reason: Additive, but touches several files: a persistent trait set plus face-slot rendering in Creature.BuildVisuals (which currently only paints body/limbs), preservation across PlayerController.Evolve and Creature.Evolve, full copy into Companion at spawn, clearing on Die, and a grant hook in EnemyAI where the "trait_miniboss" role is already detected in ApplyContent — that existing role label and the content-driven fields (contentId, role, carriesColour) mean the guardian side is half-wired and cheaper than it looks. Terrain gating would need a new passability check against BiomeTerrain/biomes.json.

findings.name: Alpha lair and the two-gate unlock
findings.statement: Each biome contains one visible Alpha lair landmark that stays empty until both gates are met: a count of distinct forms taken in that biome and a count of coloured prey eaten there (Prairies 3/15, Wetlands 5/20, Mountains 7/25, Beach 9/30, Volcanic 11/35). At 90% of both gates the lair stirs.
findings.observable_behaviour: The lair is visible on arrival but inert; meeting only the eat-count or only the form count leaves it inert; at 90% of both it visibly stirs, and on clearing both the Alpha appears.
findings.data_contract: biomes.json: distinct-forms gate and prey-eaten gate per biome; run state: per-biome distinct forms and prey-eaten counters
findings.acceptance_test: Gate table: Prairies 3 distinct/15 prey (15 reachable forms, 5.0× slack), Wetlands 5/20 (20, 4.0×), Mountains 7/25 (25, 3.6×), Beach 9/30 (25, 2.8×), Volcanic 11/35 (25, 2.3×).

findings.name: Breeding, litters and rank gain

Offspring inherit rank, all traits, emblems and panels; what varies is which colours their limbs are born loaded with, always at Pale — committed (monochrome) or flexible (mixed). Limbs cap at six, and rank is gained only this way, never by eating.

findings.name: Combat pacing invariant (2–3 pounces, no one-shots)
findings.statement: Stat tuning must keep a knockdown at 2–3 pounces against appropriate targets and more when mismatched, and must never allow a one-shot: the player's Damage is lower than every prey Health bar at every rank.
findings.observable_behaviour: Appropriate prey always requires at least two pounces to knock down; no single pounce ever knocks a prey creature straight into the dizzy state at any rank.
findings.acceptance_test: For every rank, player Damage < every prey Health bar; knockdown of an appropriate target takes 2–3 pounces.

findings.reasoning: The knockdown/dizzy/eat loop that the invariant is about does exist (EnemyAI with DownedDuration, "dizzy / vulnerable", GetEaten; Creature.isDowned/TakeDamage), so the mechanical substrate is present. But nothing in the inventory addresses the pacing *invariant* itself: there is no per-rank stat table driving player damage against prey health, no clamp or assertion that player damage stays below the smallest prey Health bar, and no validator. The one content validator, Editor/ContentCheck.cs, exposes only RollSamples/Verify/HasSpawn and prints spawn-table results ("(grazer)", "rolled: ", "RESULT: OK"), i.e. it checks biome spawn coverage, not combat numbers. Player damage instead comes from a free-floating biteDamage/BaseDamage plus unbounded-looking "upgrade_damage" purchases and ClassProfile.damageMult, while enemy health comes from ContentDatabase/EnemyAI.ApplyContent and GameConfig multipliers (Boss.HealthMultiplier, Ecology.ContactDamageScale) — two independent tuning paths with no cross-check, so no code guarantees 2–3 pounces or forbids a one-shot. I treat this as ABSENT rather than UNCONSUMED because the requirement's own 'data implied' is none: what is missing is the enforcement/check, not just a file hookup. No arena, no dormancy, no cross-run Bestiary count, no true ending. forms.json (which contains the rank rows) is parsed by FormTable/FormDef code but never loaded.
findings.effort_reason: Needs a new non-biome Ascension domain and entry condition tied to limb count (no limb/rank breeding system is visible — rank is currently kill-count Evolve), a cross-run persisted Bestiary with a distinct-form counter and a ≥100/150 gate, a dormant/awake Apex state machine and a true-ending flow, plus rewiring or deleting the kill-interval boss spawn in EcosystemManager/GameConfig.Boss. findings.name: The Bestiary screen
findings.statement: A single Bestiary screen shows rows = limb count (1–6) and columns = family (5); each of the 30 cells opens into that family's intensity ladder (Pale → Dusk → Deep → Clash → Rage) for 150 forms total. Reached forms show in full colour with their authored name, unreached ones as dark silhouettes; the screen also lists every emblem ever taken. It opens from the pause and main menus, its header shows discovered / total and the next milestone, forms found this run are highlighted with Alpha-threshold progress, and offspring the player did not pick appear outlined as known but unachieved.
findings.observable_behaviour: Opening the Bestiary from either menu shows a 6×5 grid; clicking a cell reveals five intensity entries; a newly eaten form flips from silhouette to named colour art; declining an offspring adds an outlined entry; the header reads e.g. discovered/150 and the next unlock.
findings.data_contract: Persisted Bestiary: discovered form ids, emblems claimed, per-run highlight set
findings.acceptance_test: 30 cells × 5 intensities = 150 forms displayed.

findings.observable_behaviour: Dying returns the player to a one-limb blank cube with no traits or panels, yet the Bestiary still shows every form and emblem discovered before the death, including in the run just lost.

There is no Bestiary class, no save/load type, no discovered-form registry, and no UI screen for a 6x5 grid or intensity ladder; the only death-related code is GameManager's DeathPanel/RestartButton flow plus PlayerController.Die, which restart a run without recording anything. Partially offset because FormDef/FormTable and forms.json already encode family/intensity/rank/id/name/base_hex — the catalogue side only needs wiring, not authoring.

findings.name: Record milestone unlocks
findings.statement: Discovery count pays out unlocks: 5 = Hatch-choice (start as any discovered Pale form instead of the blank), 15 = Inherited instinct (begin each run holding one earned trait), 35 = Hatch-choice extends to Dusk forms, 60 = Litter floor +1 (no litter smaller than three), 100 = the Apex wakes, 135 = Ancient skin, 150 = The Whole Beast (Genesis skin, save marked 100%).
findings.observable_behaviour: With 5 forms recorded the run-start screen offers discovered Pale forms; with 15 the new cube already carries one trait; with 60 a bare gate clear yields three offspring instead of two; at 150 the save reads 100% and the Genesis skin is selectable.
findings.data_contract: Persisted unlock flags keyed to discovered-form thresholds
findings.acceptance_test: The first rung is 5 forms — inside what a losing first run banks before meeting an Alpha.

findings.reasoning: The milestone ladder needs three things: a persisted discovered-forms count, threshold flags, and consumers of those flags (hatch-choice at run start, an inherited trait, litter floor, Apex gating, skins). None of the three appear. There is no save/meta type at all — the only cross-session-looking string is "gene_points" in PlayerController, which sits next to "upgrade_damage"/"upgrade_speed"/"upgrade_health" and is clearly the in-run upgrade currency, not a discovery record. GameManager builds a MenuPanel with a single "INITIALIZE" StartButton and a DeathPanel with "NEW EVOLUTION", so there is no run-start form-choice surface for a 5-form unlock to populate, and no Bestiary screen where discovered/total or the next milestone could be shown. Nothing gates a final boss on a cross-run count: EcosystemManager/GameConfig.Boss drive bosses off SpawnIntervalKills, an in-run kill counter, so the Apex-wakes rung has no hook either. Litter/offspring exists only as PlayerController's "OFFSPRING SPAWNED!" plus Companion.index — no litter-size floor concept. Critically, forms.json (132 KB, the 150 forms whose discovery the thresholds count) is parsed by nothing: FormTable/FormDef declare the shape and expose Load, but no caller appears, so even the denominator of the ladder is unwired. Nothing in this area contradicts the design — it is simply not built, so nothing must be deleted.
findings.what_exists_instead: Only per-run progression: PlayerController tracks totalKills, level, score, Evolve/RegisterKill and spends "gene_points" on upgrade_damage/speed/health; GameConfig.Boss spawns bosses every SpawnIntervalKills within a run. GameManager's menus are a bare INITIALIZE/NEW EVOLUTION pair with no bestiary or unlock UI. FormTable.Load and forms.json describe the 150-form space but are never read, and there is no persistence layer of any kind.
findings.effort_reason: Needs a new persistence layer (discovered-form set + unlock flags surviving death), a discovery recorder wired into Creature/EnemyAI eat-and-evolve paths, and five distinct consumers spread across systems: a run-start hatch-choice screen in GameManager's procedurally built MenuPanel, starting-trait injection in PlayerController, a litter-size floor around the OFFSPRING/Companion path, an Apex gate in EcosystemManager/GameConfig.Boss, and two cosmetic skins. Partly cheaper than it looks: FormTable/FormDef already parse forms.json's id/family/intensity/rank, so the identity keys and the 150-form denominator are ready once something calls FormTable.Load.

findings.name: Generator invariants and seed refusal
findings.statement: At generation time the generator must guarantee five invariants and refuse the seed otherwise: (1) every trait gate in a biome has a reachable carrier outside the terrain that trait unlocks; (2) the rolled palette contains enough distinct families to keep the reachable pool at least ~1.5× the form gate (min_distinct_colours = 4 in Prairies/Wetlands/Mountains, 5 in Beach and Volcanic); (3) standing population plus respawn can supply the biome's coloured-prey count with margin; (4) the plausible most-eaten colour is present in that biome's Alpha roster; (5) a trait required by a later biome remains obtainable given the expected trait set on entry.
findings.observable_behaviour: No generated biome can be entered in a state where a required trait carrier is behind its own gate, where the form gate is unclearable, or where prey run out; failing rolls are rejected and re-rolled rather than shipped.
findings.data_contract: biomes.json: min_distinct_colours, population/respawn, Alpha roster, gate thresholds
findings.acceptance_test: A 3-family Volcanic roll would clear the 11-form gate (3 × 5 = 15) but collapse slack from 2.3× to 1.36×, so it is refused.

Assets/Scripts/Content/WorldTables.cs / GameConfig.BiomeData.enemyColors — static per-biome colour lists rather than a per-run rolled palette validated against min_distinct_colours
No symbols anywhere for traits/gates (no Fins/Claws/Coat/Heat, no gate threshold or carrier-reachability members) and no Alpha-roster validation members
findings.reasoning: The only thing in the codebase resembling invariant checking is the editor-only tool ContentCheck (RollSamples / Verify / HasSpawn), which samples ContentDatabase.RollSpawn per biome and reports whether the expected colour families have spawn entries, printing "RESULT: PROBLEMS FOUND". That touches the spirit of invariants 2 and 3 (colour coverage / spawnability) but it is an offline, human-invoked report on the static JSON, not a generation-time guard that refuses a seed and re-rolls. None of the five stated rules are implemented as specified: there is no per-run palette roll subject to min_distinct_colours (4 in Prairies/Wetlands/Mountains, 5 in Beach/Volcanic) and no ~1.5x slack computation against a form gate; there is no trait system at all (no Fins/Claws/Coat/Heat symbols, no gate or carrier-reachability members), so invariants 1 and 5 have nothing to check; there is no population-plus-respawn margin math against a coloured-prey count; and there is no Alpha-roster membership test for the plausible most-eaten colour. The seed is only logged ("[Run] seed {runSeed}"), never rejected. Inventory cannot show whether biomes.json actually carries min_distinct_colours or gate thresholds, but no reader symbol for such fields appears in ContentDatabase, so any such fields are effectively unconsumed.
findings.what_exists_instead: An editor menu tool (ContentCheck.Verify) that samples ContentDatabase.RollSpawn per biome and prints OK / PROBLEMS FOUND for colour-family spawn coverage, plus static per-biome colour lists in WorldTables/GameConfig.BiomeData.enemyColors. Runs log a seed but never validate or reject it.
findings.effort_reason: Four of five invariants have no substrate: traits/gates and carrier reachability do not exist as types or fields anywhere, and there is no per-run palette roll object to validate (colours are static tables). Closing the gap means introducing a run-generation step with a reject/re-roll loop, per-biome min_distinct_colours and gate thresholds read from biomes.json, respawn/population margin math, and Alpha-roster lookups. The one cheap piece is ContentCheck.Verify/HasSpawn/RollSamples: that sampling logic is already the right shape for invariants 2-3 and could be lifted out of Editor into the runtime generator instead of rewritten.

findings.name: Unity MCP editor bridge
findings.statement: A custom Unity Editor plugin (MCPBridge.cs / MCPBridgeWindow.cs) listens on a local socket only and exposes write_file, refresh_assets, play and get_components; agents write only to Assets/Scripts/ and docs/ (never binaries), and validation is asset refresh, then grepping ~/Library/Logs/Unity/Editor.log for 'error CS' as the source of truth, then Play mode. The bridge is unreachable during domain reload and callers must wait and re-ping.
findings.observable_behaviour: Issuing write_file then refresh_assets over the local socket updates the project; during domain reload pings fail for a bounded window and then succeed; compile errors are found in Editor.log rather than the bridge's own log.
findings.acceptance_test: The bridge is unreachable for 8–13 s during domain reload, so agents wait and re-ping.

findings.reasoning: Both files named in the design exist and expose exactly the four required commands plus ping/pong for re-probing after domain reload. MCPBridge has a listener/accept loop with a Port constant and a main-thread queue (FlushMainThreadQueue) — the standard shape for an editor-side socket server that goes dead across domain reload; MCPBridgeWindow gives the status/start/stop UI. WriteFile, RefreshAssets, SetPlayMode and GetComponents are present as members, matching the write→refresh→play validation loop. GetLogs reads an Editor.log file, i.e. the log file is treated as the source of truth rather than the bridge's own buffer, as specified. Two things the inventory cannot confirm: whether the listener is bound to loopback only ('local socket only'), and whether GetLogs/agents filter for 'error CS'. One visible deviation is cosmetic-but-real: the Editor.log path literal is the Linux location ".config/unity3d/Editor.log", not the document's "~/Library/Logs/Unity/Editor.log" — a platform constant, not a mechanism difference. The bridge also exposes extra commands (create_gameobject, set_transform, set_parent, add_component, destroy_gameobject, batch) beyond the four listed; these are additions, and the design's 'agents write only to Assets/Scripts/ and docs/, never binaries' is a process constraint that the inventory gives no evidence of being enforced in code (no visible path allow-list in WriteFile).
findings.what_exists_instead: A WebSocket-over-HTTP editor bridge on a local port with the four required commands present plus a superset of scene-manipulation commands; Editor.log is read from the Linux path rather than the macOS path named in the GDD.
findings.effort_reason: The mechanism is already built; closing the residual gaps is a one-line platform-aware Editor.log path (the value is already parsed and used, just under the Linux location) and, if the write allow-list is genuinely absent, a short prefix check inside the existing WriteFile method.
